And this is a letter of the same date from the Republika Srpska minister for justice, Momcilo Mandic, to the Serbian municipalities of Hadzici and Ilidza. Mr. Banduka, I'd like you to take a moment to just read this letter in full and let me know when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. So Mr. Mandic here states that there are 90 people of Muslim ethnicity imprisoned in the Hadzici sports centre. He orders that they be transferred to the prison at Butmir and he highlights the irregularities occurring in connection with the arrests of Muslim individuals. Now, this document does not suggest that these people are being held voluntarily for their own protection, does it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: No, but we don't know who these persons are. Maybe these are persons who had been questioned by the police and then it was established that they were supposed to be prosecuted. I think, as far as I can remember now after so many years, that an attempt had been made to transfer these persons from Hadzici to Kula. However, then the airport was under the control of the international forces and one could go through the airport area only with their consent. As far as I can remember, they were driven from there and then returned for some reason. And then they were staying there temporarily only until they were transferred to Kula, that is to say to the prison there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Banduka.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. McKenna. You have re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, Excellency, but I'm afraid eight minutes is not enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll continue tomorrow, but start your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Banduka, it was suggested to you today on page 94 that the authorities in some municipalities were resisting the imposition of proper order and this was ascribed to General Sipcic. Where was General Sipcic's headquarters at the time?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: I didn't even know the general. I know the name and I think that the corps headquarters was in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did General Sipcic come to visit Hadzici at the time?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We had another document where General Galic had certain objections in relation to the late Radic. What can you tell us about agreement or tensions between the civilian and military authorities in different municipalities?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the right expression would be, tensions or lack of agreement. There was lack of agreement and there was misunderstanding, at least that's the way it looked to us. Often members of the military, or rather, military commands -- well, wanted to interfere in the work of the civilian organs and to give their own opinions and exercise their own influence. There were misunderstandings along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it the other way around as well? Did the municipal authorities sometimes believe that they had certain rights in respect of their own brigade?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Objectively speaking there were such cases because it was hard to provide the army with food, clothing, et cetera. So some individuals thought that if they were providing supplies to the army they could exercise a bit of influence in the situation in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How would you view that, these accusations that were exchanged, would you just take it all at face value?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: No, all of this was subjective, especially in the beginning of the war. This was a state of chaos, at least in our area. See, we are talking about the army. What kind of army was that in the first place? These were just people who were protecting their homes. I mean, in the beginning it was impossible to speak of any kind of army, even in the civilian organs a state was falling apart, government organs were falling apart, a war had broken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your view, is the police part of the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What are they?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know the police was organised through the Ministry of the Interior; that is to say, the minister was at the top of this system of organisation, and then from the top orders were issued. They had this kind of jurisdiction. So all the way down to the municipality it was the minister and his services and the assistant ministers that had certain powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness Music was mentioned and on page 12854 he said that Tihomir Glavas was from the SDS. Was Tihomir Glavas a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: As far as I know, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we please take a look at D1074. This document was admitted when Mr. Glavas testified, pages 92 and 93. This is a document of his, so could you please take a look at subparagraph (a) where he speaks about similar things, things that are similar to what Galic and Sipcic referred to. So if you look at (a) and then the first two sentences?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Foundation.

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what does he say here? Who are these free agents that enjoy the support of the authorities?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of free agents he's referring to. Probably there were some. He says here that there weren't any significant paramilitary units there. So this was probably a reference to small groups or individuals who were difficult. It was hard to make them part of a regular established formation like the army or police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Such individuals, did they enjoy the support of the Hadzici municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: No, we just had problems with such individuals and such small groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please. I think that it's the next page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The fourth paragraph. "As mentioned above, small groups and individuals, so-called 'free agents,' committed the crime of theft from other persons, mainly movable property and assets ..." Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this means in our language, "free agent"?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Well, a free agent -- well, it's the word itself that is very telling. "Free," meaning not being under anybody's command or control. Well, we have an expression for such people but I wouldn't like to use it here. So these are people who are not part of the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move two pages ahead, please. Could we leaf through the document in this way. Can we have page 4 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this, the third paragraph, "From the 1st of August, 1992, when a large number of police officers returned from the front line to the police station, they were engaged in the regular MUP activities ...," and further down it says: "In that period, a certain number of crimes and perpetrators were detected ..." Did you have any knowledge or experience to that effect? What means did you have available for prosecution when the police was on the front line?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Well, we had that number of policemen that were not at the front line. These were units, or rather, these were individuals who could, but there were very few of them, especially in 1992. We were seriously decimated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll read out item (d): "As regards the treatment and competency to guard prisoners. It can be said that we had a large number of detained persons who once they were interviewed and after other relevant information had been gathered were taken to the state prison in Kula or released. A small number of those brought in, currently 11, are in the prison in Hadzici and they are being treated properly and in accordance with the law. We would also like to note that in the area of Hadzici municipality we did not have collection camps used by the army to bring in Muslim population without documents under reasons for detention." Mr. Banduka, what we could hear from Aviljas and Mandic, to what extent is it confirmed by a document produced by the chief of police in Hadzici, is there a difference or is it mutually corroborative?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: Of course there is a difference. The chief of police was in Hadzici on the spot. I think Mr. Mandic never even saw Hadzici and the same goes for Mr. Aviljas. Therefore, it is logical and I believe that the man who wrote this document, who was in the area, was far better aware of the situation and had better information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can look at the first page. The date is the 9th of August, 1991. Mr. Banduka --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- until when were there civilians in the sports centre and when were they exchanged so that there were no more civilians left?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: I've answered that already. I think that by August there were no civilians left in the sports centre. There was one situation, though, when there was an exchange. In other words, there were people who were still living in their homes but wanted to go to Muslim territory or the other way around. So civilians were occasionally exchanged at Kobiljaca, and if an exchange fell through people would return, and we used that area as a sort of staging area where they would await their departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if there was someone there in October or in November, that person was not a civilian?

utterances.speaker: VIDOMIR BANDUKA
utterances.text: I don't think they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this conclude the day or should I go to another P document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll stop here. Mr. Banduka, we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. I'd like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of February, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.49 p.m.,
